newsitem.title: ITALY: Castro to visit Rome, Italian agencies say.
newsitem.headline: Castro to visit Rome, Italian agencies say.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro will visit Rome next month to attend a summit organised by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO), Italian news agencies reported on Tuesday.
The agencies, quoting diplomatic sources in the Italian capital, said Castro would stay for a week. They gave no further details and official confirmation was not immediately available.
Diplomatic sources have said Castro is expected to meet Pope John Paul if he attends for the November 13-17 world food summit organised by the Rome-based FAO.
If the meeting went ahead, they said, Castro was likely to invite the Pope to Cuba, the only Spanish-speaking country in Latin America which the Pontiff has not yet visited.
Vatican Foreign Minister Jean Louis Tauran earlier ended a visit to Cuba during which he met Castro late on Monday. He refused to comment on his talks with the Cuban leader.

Tauran, an archbishop, was the first Vatican foreign minister invited to Cuba by the island's communist authorities and his visit reflected improved relations between the Cuban government and the Roman Catholic church.
